edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: EPA and DHA lower hepatic VLDL production, shift membrane lipid signaling, and can modestly dampen inflammatory eicosanoid tone. Those mechanisms matter most for Cardiovascular disease when baseline triglycerides are high or the outcome is tightly linked to cardiometabolic inflammation.
edges.summary: In general adult, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that omega-3 in adults with normal triglycerides tracks with lower risk of cardiovascular disease. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
